measured.heard: The program sets N to 2 and switches on N. Case 2 has no break. The scenes that follow answer this question, one output line at a time. A switch jumps to the case label, whose value matches the controlling expression. With N equals 2, that is case 2 which prints 2. A case label is only a label. It does not stop execution. So the switch falls through into case 3 and prints 3. A break statement ends the smallest enclosing switch or loop. Here that is the switch. After the switch ends, the program prints done. With break.c adds a break after case 1 and after case 2. So no case runs on into the next case. With N equals 2, with break.c prints only 2 from the switch, and then done. Compiled by GCC 16 with W extra. Fall through.c gets a warning that the statements on line 7 and 9 may fall through, and with break.c gets none. Into break.c is fall through.c with case 3 cut down to a loan break. With N equals 2 at prints 2, falls into case 3, whose break ends the switch, and then prints done. For into break.c, GCC 16 with W extra still warns at line 7, where case 1 falls into case 2, but says nothing at line 9, where case 2 falls into a case that only breaks. Apple clang with W extra gives no fall through warning for any of the 3 programs. A case label only marks where execution enters a switch. It never ends a case. In fall through.c, the break on line 12 is what ends the switch.
